## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `161653aed2ee5d28e2db9f09d5ebbcc64a7ffcd5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/index.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/default-export-retired.pin.test.ts + packages/drivers/driver-memory/package.json, packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts, packages/core/src/types.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-registration.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/verify/src/harness.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and on `.changeset/26206-driver-memory-default.md`). Inputs: card #26206 body and its 13 comments, PR #27323 body, file list (4 paths, +58/-18) and net diff against `main`, the head's 45 check-runs, and the cited code read on `origin/main` at `19f49ef354`. The changeset and README were read to judge ② and are not reviewed under ④.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 18 success, 14 skipped, 13 in progress, 0 failure. Green and relevant: `Check Changeset` (this job runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major`), `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Check PR Size`. Still in progress: `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not pre-empt them, and the seat lands only on all-green.

### ① Derived judgments

The published surface is the root entry alone: `packages/drivers/driver-memory/package.json` `exports` has one key, `.`, with `import` → `dist/index.mjs` / `dist/index.d.mts` and `require` → `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts`, both generated by tsup from `src/index.ts`. So every change to `src/index.ts`'s export statements is a change to what is published, on both conditions.

1. **Removed from the published entry: the `default` export** (the legacy `{ id, version, onEnable }` object). Reaches: the ESM `import x from '@objectstack/driver-memory'` binding, the TypeScript-under-CJS `esModuleInterop` default binding, `require('@objectstack/driver-memory').default`, and `import('@objectstack/driver-memory')` then `.default`. All four lose a value they had on `main`. **Right** to name this a narrowing of the published surface and BREAKING; the PR does so.
2. **Every named export stays** (22 value and type exports: `InMemoryDriver`, `InMemoryStrategy`, `FileSystemPersistenceAdapter`, `LocalStoragePersistenceAdapter`, `MemoryAnalyticsService`, the tenancy-guard and unique-constraint helpers and their types). I diffed the export statements on `main` against the hunk: no named export moves. **Right**.
3. **Accept-set change at the string-plugin door.** `materializeStackPlugin` (`packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts:63-72`) takes `mod?.default || mod` and, for an object without `init`, calls `wrapBundle`, which `serve.ts:4708` and `verify/src/harness.ts:605` both implement as `new AppPlugin(bundle)`. On `main` the default object has `id`, so `AppPlugin`'s constructor names it `plugin.app.com.objectstack.driver.memory` and its `start()` (`app-plugin.ts:1628-1667`) runs `onEnable` with a `drivers.register` that calls `ql.registerDriver`. After this PR the module namespace carries no `manifest`, `id`, `name` or any `APP_CATEGORY_KEYS` payload, so the constructor takes the empty-env branch (`app-plugin.ts:454-491`): `name = 'plugin.app.empty-empty'`, `requiresServices = []`, and `init()` logs at `debug`, which the CLI's `warn` floor discards. So `plugins: ['@objectstack/driver-memory']` moves from "registers an `InMemoryDriver`" to "registers nothing, says nothing". The PR body and changeset name this. **Right**, and it is the one behavioural narrowing beyond the import binding; judged under ③.
4. **Not a metadata-protocol change.** No `*.zod.ts`, no object definition, no stored shape, no authorable key moves; `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Right**.
5. **The type surface the CJS condition publishes** (`dist/index.d.ts`) loses its `export default` line, which is what `FalseExportDefault` measured: the `.d.ts` said `export default X` while the CJS build put X on `.default`. With no default in source, tsup emits neither, so the attw finding disappears by construction, not by configuration. **Right**, and it is the card's acceptance.
6. The dev's PR body says the four sibling drivers (`driver-sql`, `driver-mongodb`, `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `driver-turso`) keep the identical legacy default; confirmed on `main` (`src/index.ts` of each has `export default {`). They are out of this card's acceptance and the PR does not touch them. **Right** not to widen.

### ② Semver level

`patch` with a BREAKING banner is this repo's rule for this diff, and the declaration lines match it.

- AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." The workflow prose the author is pointed to (`pr-automation.yml:775-779`) spells the same: `Metadata-protocol: none` covers "drivers, services … `feat:` and `fix!:` alike → `patch`".
- `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, the level axis: a declared `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch`. The changeset grades `'@objectstack/driver-memory': patch`. The launch-window guard forbids `major`; none is declared. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head, and that job also runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right value per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:111-118`: "`no (narrowing)` — NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm." The diff widens nothing and removes a published runtime export, so the arm is owed, and the claim's bare `no` (comment 6473747892) was the under-declared form; the dev's amendment is correct and the dogfood battery the arm triggers was run on this head per the report.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/driver-memory#default)`, the category built for a retired published runtime export (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:4397-4470`). Operand `default` is an identifier under `EXPORT_SPELLING_RE`, predicate 2 now reads a `default` operand through the import arm only (`defaultImportReference`, #26324, the blocker this card waited on), and predicate 3 wants the FROM block to name exactly the operand: the body carries one line, `- FROM `default` TO …`, which names it. The gate's own verdict is the `Check Changeset` success above.
- BREAKING banner present (`**BREAKING** (a runtime export is removed)`), FROM → TO line present, no staged window claimed, which is right for a startup-stage removal (the import either resolves or it does not; there is nothing to stage).

No disagreement with the declared level or lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The open question**, verbatim from the report: "After this lands, a stack config that writes plugins: ['@objectstack/driver-memory'] silently registers nothing: materializeStackPlugin (packages/core/src/stack-plugins.ts:65) wraps the default-less module namespace into an AppPlugin that takes its no-id, no-payload branch. … Should the string-entry door refuse that loudly?"

**Answer: yes, the door should refuse loudly, and that refusal is a core change outside this card. Option A, with one tightening: the follow-up card is filed now, on the dev's seam reading, not conditionally after a later `os serve` measurement.** Reasons, read against the tree and the repo's principles:

1. **What this PR makes worse, that a user can reach today.** On `main`, `plugins: ['@objectstack/driver-memory']` registers a memory driver at `start()`; after this PR the same line boots an empty `AppPlugin` named `plugin.app.empty-empty` and registers no driver. That is a real regression of a reachable spelling. Its reach is bounded: the README on `main` already labelled the default "legacy … not a kernel `Plugin`; register through `DriverPlugin`", no example, scaffold template, doc page or skill writes the string form (I re-ran the search on `origin/main`: 0 string `plugins` entries, 0 default bindings, the 3 dynamic imports destructure `InMemoryDriver`), and `cloud` / `hotcrm` are not measured. The changeset names the replacement in the `plugins` array, and an instance entry passes `materializeStackPlugin` untouched (`DriverPlugin` has `init`), so the prescription is correct.
2. **It is not silent everywhere, and where it was loudest it never worked.** `serve.ts:5493-5545`'s no-storage boot guard judges "by the end of plugin init". The legacy `onEnable` ran in `start()`, after that judgement, so on a production boot with no `OS_DATABASE_URL` under the `single` posture the string spelling was already refused before this PR, and on other production boots the guard already printed its one line and let the boot go on. What changes is the step after: before, a driver then arrived in `start()`; after, the first query fails on a missing driver. Loud, but late, and not at the door that was declared.
3. **The defect is in core and is not specific to this package.** `mod?.default || mod` is precisely the lenient `||` fallback Prime Directive #12 forbids in a consumer, and `AppPlugin`'s empty-env branch exists for a different caller (an empty environment artifact) and is reached here by accident. Any string entry naming a module with no default and no `init` takes the same path today. Prime Directive #10 says file an issue for a contract violation and never bury it; the dev's seam probe is already the measurement the card needs (a `wrapBundle` that received a namespace with no `id` and no `onEnable`), so "a seat measures through `os serve` and, if it holds, files" defers a card whose evidence exists. File it against `materializeStackPlugin`: a string entry whose module has no default and no `init` is refused by name, with the one-line fix. That is the "declared capability must not silently do nothing" principle applied at the right seam, and it closes the hole for every default-less package at once.
4. **Why not B.** The claim's file surface (6473747892) is `packages/drivers/driver-memory/**` and one changeset, "no other package"; a core change on this PR breaches it. The refusal rule is also a contract decision on the string-plugin door (`stack-plugins.ts` header: "its default export (or, failing that, the module itself) is the plugin"), which is the seat's or the maintainer's to make, not something to settle inside a driver card. Holding a 0-known-producer narrowing on that decision buys nothing the follow-up card does not.

**Escalation flag for the seat, not a hold:** whether the string spelling `plugins: ['@objectstack/driver-memory']` was ever a supported door, or only an accident of the legacy default, decides how the follow-up card is worded (refuse, or refuse-and-name-`DriverPlugin`). Either way this PR's changeset already tells that reader what to write.

No other boundary crossed: no package added or removed, no `exports` key changed, no `.github/**`, no `ui/`, no governed path.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/index.ts`
- The hunk removes lines 64-80 on `main` (the `export default { id, version, onEnable }` block) and replaces them with a seven-line comment. Against the card's acceptance ("0 `FalseExportDefault`"): the finding is "the `.d.ts` declares `export default` but the CJS build does not return it from `require()`". With no `export default` in the only source of both conditions' output, tsup emits no `default` in `dist/index.js` and no `export default` in `dist/index.d.ts` / `dist/index.d.mts`, so the finding cannot recur from this tree. Holds by construction; the PR body's attw run is consistent with it but is not what I judged.
- Against the code it cites: the comment says the object "was not a kernel `Plugin` (the contract is init/start/destroy)"; `packages/core/src/types.ts:155` `Plugin` requires `name` and lifecycle methods, and the object had `id` / `onEnable`. Correct. It names `new DriverPlugin(new InMemoryDriver(), 'memory')` from `@objectstack/runtime`; `driver-plugin.ts:34-37` takes exactly `(driver, driverName?)`. Correct.
- `InMemoryDriver` was imported at line 2 for both the named re-export and the default's `onEnable`; the re-export keeps it live, so no unused import is left (ESLint is green on the head).
- Tried to break it: the empty-AppPlugin path above is the only behavioural reach, judged under ③. No other reader of `default` in this package's tests or in the repo (0 default bindings; the two `mod.default ?? mod` hits in driver-memory tests are sql.js, not this entry).

`packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/default-export-retired.pin.test.ts`
- Case 1 pins `'default' in entry === false` over `import * as entry from './index.js'`. Under vitest's ESM namespace that is a true pin of the source entry; the dev's ablation (an `export default { id: 'ablated' }` at the old site made it fail) is the right shape and the report records it, but the tree alone shows the pin is live: the namespace has no `default` key unless the source exports one.
- Case 2 pins five named classes as functions and constructs `InMemoryDriver`, asserting `driver.name === 'com.objectstack.driver.memory'`. That is the replacement door the changeset names, pinned to still work. Good.
- **Should-fix (not blocking):** the pin reads `src`, so it does not itself prove the tarball shape the card's acceptance names. The structural argument above covers it, and no CI gate runs attw, but a one-line note in the test header saying the published-build claim rests on tsup generating both conditions from this entry would stop a future reader treating this test as the attw proof. Cosmetic; no code change required.
- Adding a file to `src/` is compiled by `tsc --noEmit`; the report says the typecheck program counts it once. `Type Check · workspace` is still in progress on the head; its conclusion governs.

Prose faces, read for ② only: the README drops the `default` row from Key Exports and adds "The package has no default export." `check-published-readme-exports` reads import lines and documented symbols against the built types; removing a documented symbol that no longer exists is the safe direction. The changeset carries both declaration lines, one marker, the banner and one FROM → TO line.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 1 should-fix (test-header note), plus the ③ follow-up card against `materializeStackPlugin`, which belongs to the seat, not to this diff.
